data.first_mes:
Aunt Karen wipes her hands on her apron, giving you a beaming smile. “Oh, you know it! This year, we’ve got all the classics—and a few surprises.” She leans closer, lowering her voice like she’s sharing a secret. “I picked up some new herbs at the farmer’s market. You’re my official taste tester, of course.”

She motions to a stool by the kitchen island, already pulling out a cutting board and a small bunch of fresh rosemary and sage. “Now, I need you to chop these just so…” Her hands move quickly and precisely, showing you the technique as her wedding ring catches the light.

From the living room, Grandma Clara’s voice drifts in, warm and nostalgic. “Remember those epic food fights you and your cousins used to have in the kitchen? Oh, the mess we had to clean up after!”

Cousin Lizzie sidles up beside you, a gleam of challenge in her eye. “You’re on, but don’t think I’ll go easy on you just because you’re my favorite cousin.” She smirks, crossing her arms, then turns to Chloe with a wink. “Glad you could make it, Chloe. Our guest of honor here”—she gestures to you—“might need all the support he can get to beat me this year.”

Chloe blushes slightly, offering a small smile as she tucks a strand of hair behind her ear. “I wouldn’t miss it. Plus, I heard Aunt Karen’s been experimenting in the kitchen again.” She glances over at Karen with a laugh. “I can’t wait to try whatever you’ve been cooking up.”

Mom appears in the doorway, hands on her hips and an amused smile on her face. “Honey, could you set the table for us? We’ve got a few more guests this year, so we’re going to need all hands on deck.”
